title: SaasReport: Stripe reports for every stakeholder
description: Install once and every person who asks about your Stripe numbers gets the report built for them, on a schedule, with findings that show their working.
status: SaasReport is in development and is not yet listed in the Stripe App Marketplace. Every figure on this page comes from the engine running on made-up sample data, and says so.

hero.headline: The right Stripe report for each person who asks.
hero.sub: Your finance lead, your board, your support desk and your investors all ask different questions of the same data. SaasReport builds each of them their own report, on a schedule, from Stripe alone.

problem.title: One dashboard cannot answer every question

points.title: Everyone asks something different
points.text: The founder wants growth and leaks, finance wants the revenue base, support wants failed payments and refunds. A single view serves none of them well.

points.title: Reports are assembled by hand
points.text: Someone exports, pastes into a sheet, builds charts and writes the commentary, again every week, month and quarter.

points.title: Numbers drift between people
points.text: When each report is built separately, two people can quote different figures for the same month and nobody can say which is right.

solution.title: Install once. Each stakeholder gets their own report.

steps.title: Connect Stripe
steps.text: Install the app. It asks to read; it never changes anything in your account.

steps.title: Reports run on a cadence
steps.text: Daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual reports are built for the last complete period.

steps.title: Figures are computed, not written
steps.text: Every number comes from a published rule over your Stripe data. The same input gives the same figure every time.

steps.title: Findings show their working
steps.text: A finding is a published rule applied to those figures. It states the numbers that triggered it and a suggested next step. No model decides a number.

steps.title: People see what their Stripe role allows
steps.text: Access follows the person's Stripe role. A role that cannot see refunds in Stripe cannot see the refunds report.

sectors.title: Who it is for
sectors.note: Each card says what exists in the engine today. Nothing here is a claim about customers.

items.name: Subscription software
items.text: Recurring revenue and how it moved: new, expanded, contracted and churned, retention, payment failures, refunds and disputes.

items.name: Merchants without subscriptions
items.text: Payment volume, failures, refunds by reason and disputes, for the people who handle them.

items.name: Marketplaces and platforms
items.text: The operator sees platform fees and take rate from the platform account. Stripe does not let an app installed by a platform read its merchants' accounts, so each merchant installs SaasReport on its own account to get its own reports. A platform can recommend it; it cannot pull merchant data through its install.
items.status: Operator report in the engine; merchant referral not built

tryit.title: Pick a stakeholder and see the report
tryit.note: Sample data. A made-up account, a made-up month and the month before it. The figures, changes and findings are produced by the same engine that will run on real accounts.

access.title: Who sees what
access.text: Choose Stripe roles. A person's access is the union of what their Stripe roles can see. A role not listed, or a user whose roles cannot be verified, sees nothing.
access.none: No report: none of these roles can see the data behind any report.

roi.title: What your reporting costs you today
roi.note: This is arithmetic on your own inputs. It makes no claim about how much time SaasReport saves you; the last slider is your own assumption.

commitments.note: Each line is a commitment in the registry with its status. Planned means it is a design commitment that is not yet built or proven.
